name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [ROCm] Compile IFRT IR MPMD programs on PJRT-backed IFRT clients

head_commit.message:
Compile IFRT IR MPMD programs on PJRT-backed IFRT clients

`compile_mpmd` compiled IFRT IR programs with the client's default
compiler. On PJRT-backed IFRT clients, such as the CPU client and PJRT
plugin clients, that is `PjRtCompiler`, which only accepts HLO
programs, so compiling any MPMD program failed with "PjRtCompiler
requires an HloProgram".

On those clients, compile with XLA's `IfrtIrProgramCompiler` instead.
It compiles each atom program through the client with
`BasicAtomProgramCompiler`, and the resulting executable runs the
program with the IFRT IR interpreter. Other clients still use their
default compiler.

`_sdy_mpmd` also imported `jax.jaxlib._jax`, which does not exist in
jaxlib wheels, so importing `jaxlib._sdy_mpmd` failed. It now imports
`jaxlib._jax`, as it already does for `jaxlib._hlo`.

The new `tests/sdy_mpmd_test.py` compiles and runs a program over two
single-device meshes on the CPU client.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Allow `tmem_alloc` ops of up to 576 columns on sm_107f.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Allow `tmem_alloc` ops of up to 576 columns on sm_107f.

On sm_107f, TMEM allocations of more than
512 columns are lowered to an exclusive allocation of all 576 columns. However,
the `tmem_alloc` verifier still capped allocations at 512 columns, so such
allocations could not be expressed with WG semantics.

The verifier now derives the column limit from the architecture recorded on the
enclosing module: 576 columns on sm_107f and 512 everywhere else, including
when the module carries no architecture. Layout inference also gives slices of
a `tmem_alloc` (`slice_tmem`) the same default layout as the allocation itself,
so that TMEM buffers carved out of a merged allocation don't need an explicit
layout.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Allow allocating up to 576 TMEM columns on sm_107f.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Allow allocating up to 576 TMEM columns on sm_107f.

On sm_107f, TMEM has 576 columns per CTA
instead of 512, but the columns past 512 can only be used through
`tcgen05.alloc.exclusive`, which must be the only TMEM allocation that exists
at any time and must be released with `tcgen05.dealloc.exclusive`.

TMEM allocations of more than 512 columns are now lowered to an exclusive
allocation of all 576 columns on sm_107f. Since nothing else can be allocated
alongside an exclusive allocation, and while context switching
no CTAs can use the remaining 576 - 512 columns, there is no benefit to allocating fewer columns.

The mode is selected automatically from the number of columns, so
there is no new user-facing API, and allocations of at most 512 columns are
unchanged. This means that now if someone wants to use this feature on
sm107f they have to allocate once and use slice_tmem API.

Other architectures keep the 512-column limit.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [Mosaic GPU][NFC] Introduce SmemDescriptor for MMA SMEM operand slicing.

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU][NFC] Introduce SmemDescriptor for MMA SMEM operand slicing.

`mma_utils.create_descriptor` previously coupled shared-memory descriptor construction to a fixed `mma_bytewidth_k`, precomputed two-level K-group striding tuples, and a caller-facing `split_const` overload flag. This required `tcgen05` and `wgmma` to manually re-encode group and instruction byte offsets and prevented arbitrary per-step K offsets needed by upcoming variable-width MMA K steps on SM103.

Return an `SmemDescriptor` dataclass from `mma_utils.create_descriptor` exposing `encoded_offset` (for `tcgen05` inline PTX) and `slice_i64` (for `wgmma`), remove `split_const` from `create_descriptor` and `encode_descriptor`, and update `tcgen05` and `wgmma` to slice SMEM descriptors by logical `(mn_idx, k_idx)` element coordinates (collapsing `wgmma`'s outer K-group and inner instruction loops into a single per-instruction loop).

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Fix index dtype overflow for negative indices in jnp.take

head_commit.message:
Fix index dtype overflow for negative indices in jnp.take

When wrapping negative indices in jnp.take, indices + a.shape[axis_idx]
retained the dtype of indices. For small integer dtypes such as int8 with
axis lengths greater than 128, the addition overflowed in modular arithmetic,
causing negative indices to be evaluated as out-of-bounds and returning fill
values (NaN or INT_MIN). Additionally, mode='wrap' threw an OverflowError.

Use lax_utils.index_dtype_for_axis_size to upcast the index dtype appropriately
before normalizing negative indices or calculating modulo in mode='wrap'.

Fixes #42377.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Guard null contexts in MosaicGpuPrepare

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Guard null contexts in MosaicGpuPrepare

## Problem

`MosaicGpuPrepare` dereferenced `command_buffer_requests` and `collective_params` unconditionally at entry, even though both contexts default to null outside `CustomCallThunk::Prepare` or when `CollectiveParams` is omitted. Existing command buffer tests also did not verify output values or absence of the warmup execution log.

## Change

Mark `command_buffer_requests` as `absl_nullable` and guard `SetRequiresWarmup(false)` at the start of `MosaicGpuPrepare`. Validate `collective_params` and `resources` before dereferencing them, returning `InternalError` when either is null. Expand unit and B200 command buffer tests to cover null contexts, warmup log absence, first call recording, replay, and update.

## Behavior

Valid `CustomCallThunk::Prepare` runs are unchanged, while null `CommandBufferRequests` or `CollectiveParams` contexts no longer dereference null. No flag is added.

display_title: [Mosaic GPU] Guard null contexts in MosaicGpuPrepare

head_commit.message:
[Mosaic GPU] Guard null contexts in MosaicGpuPrepare

## Problem

`MosaicGpuPrepare` dereferenced `command_buffer_requests` and `collective_params` unconditionally at entry, even though both contexts default to null outside `CustomCallThunk::Prepare` or when `CollectiveParams` is omitted. Existing command buffer tests also did not verify output values or absence of the warmup execution log.

## Change

Mark `command_buffer_requests` as `absl_nullable` and guard `SetRequiresWarmup(false)` at the start of `MosaicGpuPrepare`. Validate `collective_params` and `resources` before dereferencing them, returning `InternalError` when either is null. Expand unit and B200 command buffer tests to cover null contexts, warmup log absence, first call recording, replay, and update.

## Behavior

Valid `CustomCallThunk::Prepare` runs are unchanged, while null `CommandBufferRequests` or `CollectiveParams` contexts no longer dereference null. No flag is added.

head_commit.message:
Fix `jnp.nan_to_num` double replacement of substituted values (jax-ml/jax#42406)

Fixes #42406.

Problem:
In https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/42406, `jnp.nan_to_num` calculates the infinity masks on the intermediate array `out` instead of the original input array. This means that if a `NaN` value was replaced by `jnp.inf` in the first step, it was incorrectly matched and replaced again during the positive infinity check in the second step.

Solution:
Update `jnp.nan_to_num` to compute `isnan`, `isposinf`, and `isneginf` masks on the original input array `x` rather than the intermediate `out` array. Added `testNanToNumCustomSubstitutions` in `lax_numpy_test.py` as a regression test.

head_commit.message:
[jax-buildcop] Shard `lax_scipy_special_functions_test` on TPU under `USE_MINIMAL_SHARD_COUNT` and reduce `iv` test compilations

- **Root Cause**: Following the addition of `jax.scipy.special.iv` tests to `lax_scipy_special_functions_test.py`, `Bazel tests TPU (JAX artifacts version = head) / v4-8, py3.12, libtpu=pinned, jaxlib=head` timed out in `TPU single-accelerator tests (full)`. `ci/run_bazel_test_tpu.sh` sets `--repo_env=USE_MINIMAL_SHARD_COUNT=True`, which uses `minimal_shard_count` instead of `shard_count`. Because `lax_scipy_special_functions_test` did not set `minimal_shard_count`, all 20 TPU shards ran in a single unsharded target and exceeded the 300s test timeout once the `iv` tests (~50s on TPU v4) were added.
- **Fix**:
  1. Set `minimal_shard_count = {"tpu": 8}` on `lax_scipy_special_functions_test` in `tests/BUILD` so Bazel TPU CI shards the suite across 8 shards.
  2. Reuse compiled input shapes for special-value checks in `test_iv_orders_and_regimes` and evaluate vector gradients directly in `test_iv_grad` without redundant recompilation, reducing `test_iv*` runtime on TPU v4 by ~40% (from ~50s to ~30s).

head_commit.message:
Add jax.scipy.special.iv for integer-order modified Bessel functions.

Provide `jax.scipy.special.iv(v, z)` to compute the modified Bessel function of the first kind of integer order `v` for real and complex arguments, complementing `jn` and `yn` while matching SciPy's naming convention (`in` is a Python reserved keyword).

For real arguments, orders `|v| ≤ 1` delegate to `lax.bessel_i0e` and `lax.bessel_i1e` rescaled by `exp(|z|)` using double-word `(hi, lo)` range reduction (`|z| = k * ln(2) + r` and `ldexp`) to preserve full mantissa accuracy up to the overflow threshold. Higher orders use the non-alternating power series for small arguments, Hankel's asymptotic expansion in double-word arithmetic for large arguments, and backward Miller recurrence normalized by the Neumann sum in the intermediate transition region. Complex arguments are evaluated via the connection formula `I_n(z) = i^{-n} J_n(i * z)`, with forward-mode autodiff supported via `I_v'(z) = 0.5 * (I_{v-1}(z) + I_{v+1}(z))`. Also add integer-order `iv` coverage to the Bessel ULP precision test suite.

single-device meshes on the CPU client. It is skipped before jaxlib
extension version 521, which this change introduces.

display_title: Fix index dtype overflow for negative indices in jnp.take

head_commit.message:
Fix index dtype overflow for negative indices in jnp.take

When wrapping negative indices in jnp.take, indices + a.shape[axis_idx]
retained the dtype of indices. For small integer dtypes such as int8 with
axis lengths greater than 128, the addition overflowed in modular
arithmetic, causing negative indices to be evaluated as out-of-bounds and
returning fill values (NaN or INT_MIN). Additionally, mode='wrap' raised
an OverflowError.

Upcast the index dtype with lax_utils.index_dtype_for_axis_size before
wrapping negative indices or computing the modulo in mode='wrap'.

Fixes #42377.

display_title: Add jax.scipy.special.iv for integer-order modified Bessel functions.

head_commit.message:
Add jax.scipy.special.iv for integer-order modified Bessel functions.

Provide `jax.scipy.special.iv(v, z)` to compute the modified Bessel function of the first kind of integer order `v` for real and complex arguments, complementing `jn` and `yn` while matching SciPy's naming convention (`in` is a Python reserved keyword).

For real arguments, orders `|v| ≤ 1` delegate to `lax.bessel_i0e` and `lax.bessel_i1e` rescaled by `exp(|z|)` using double-word `(hi, lo)` range reduction (`|z| = k * ln(2) + r` and `ldexp`) to preserve full mantissa accuracy up to the overflow threshold. Higher orders use the non-alternating power series for small arguments, Hankel's asymptotic expansion in double-word arithmetic for large arguments, and backward Miller recurrence normalized by the Neumann sum in the intermediate transition region. Complex arguments are evaluated via the connection formula `I_n(z) = i^{-n} J_n(i * z)`, with forward-mode autodiff supported via `I_v'(z) = 0.5 * (I_{v-1}(z) + I_{v+1}(z))`. Also add integer-order `iv` coverage to the Bessel ULP precision test suite.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

head_commit.message:
[PJRT/JAX] Preserve subnormal floats during JAX Python callbacks on CPU

When executing CPU computations, PJRT and XLA thread pools configure the CPU to flush subnormal floating-point numbers to zero to improve performance. However, when XLA calls back into Python (via `jax.pure_callback`, `io_callback`, or `buffer_callback`), this setting was left enabled on the calling thread. Python code (like NumPy) expects standard floating-point behavior, so leaving this setting enabled caused subnormal numbers to silently become zero inside user callbacks.

This change adds `tsl::port::ScopedDontFlushDenormal` and `tsl::port::ScopedSetRound(FE_TONEAREST)` to `xla::HostCallbackScope`. This ensures all Python callbacks run with standard floating-point settings, and safely restores XLA's expected settings when the callback returns.

Bumps `JAX_IFRT_VERSION_NUMBER` to 85 and adds regression tests guarded by this version.

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: Make jnp.interp match numpy.interp when fp contains infinite values

head_commit.message:
Make jnp.interp match numpy.interp when fp contains infinite values

jnp.interp returned NaN at and around knots where fp is infinite (inf - inf
and 0 * inf in the interpolation formula), where numpy.interp returns the
knot value at a knot and the signed infinity inside the interval. Where the
interpolated value is NaN and x is not, return the knot value at an exact
knot and otherwise evaluate from the other end of the interval, falling back
to the shared value when both ends are equal, as numpy's arr_interp does.
Finite inputs and their gradients are unchanged.

For complex fp, interpolate the real and imaginary parts separately, as
numpy does, so the NaN handling applies per component.

Fixes #42318

name: Bazel ROCm
display_title: [ROCm] Compile IFRT IR MPMD programs on PJRT-backed IFRT clients

head_commit.message:
Compile IFRT IR MPMD programs on PJRT-backed IFRT clients

`compile_mpmd` compiled IFRT IR programs with the client's default
compiler. On PJRT-backed IFRT clients, such as the CPU client and PJRT
plugin clients, that is `PjRtCompiler`, which only accepts HLO
programs, so compiling any MPMD program failed with "PjRtCompiler
requires an HloProgram".

On those clients, compile with XLA's `IfrtIrProgramCompiler` instead.
It compiles each atom program through the client with
`BasicAtomProgramCompiler`, and the resulting executable runs the
program with the IFRT IR interpreter. Other clients still use their
default compiler.

`_sdy_mpmd` also imported `jax.jaxlib._jax`, which does not exist in
jaxlib wheels, so importing `jaxlib._sdy_mpmd` failed. It now imports
`jaxlib._jax`, as it already does for `jaxlib._hlo`.

The new `tests/sdy_mpmd_test.py` compiles and runs a program over two
single-device meshes on the CPU client. It is skipped before jaxlib
extension version 520, which this change introduces.
